Definition: to tread in pieces, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer, or (specifically) to overlay
BiblicalUsage: Radad is to tread in pieces, to conquer — and, by a second sense, to overlay with gold. God says to Cyrus, 'I will go before thee, and make the crooked places straight: I will break in pieces the gates of brass'; David says the LORD 'subdueth my people under me'; and the Levite's journey passed Jebus as the day drew toward evening.
TheologicalSignificance: What I see here is that the treading is God's work, not mine: He subdues peoples and breaks gates of brass, and my part is to walk in the way He opens.
